tables.title: Character values
tables.description: These values belong to the current-character word at array index 1 (byte offset +0x04). The word is an ID, not a character-unlock bitmask.

tables.title: Runtime mirror fields
tables.description: The declaration is a 32-bit-word array. Multiply the array index by four to obtain a byte offset; the symbol itself is the storage base.
rows: Activation marker: the native save-start path writes 1 after copying the 0x30-byte runtime block. Other values are not assigned an enum meaning here.
Current character ID; see Character values above. This word also resides at native address 0x8015C5DC.
Current health in half-heart units. Also exported as [D_8015C5E4](./D_8015C5E4.md); the unsigned array declaration does not change the underlying health field.
Character-change/dirty marker: the character-switch path writes 1. The complete reset protocol is not established here.

tables.title: System structure fields
tables.description: Dereference this pointer once, then use these offsets from the full system structure base (0x8008CCC0 in the US executable). D_800BCCC0_BD8C0 is an interior alias 0x30000 bytes farther into the same structure.
rows: Game-loop timing/control byte; the system-step setter writes 2.
VI counter used by the saved play-time accumulator. Native Start pause does not stop its VI increments.
Game-loop/frame counter; a running numeric counter, not a state ID.
Main system step. Known entries are listed below.
Main-step completion byte. A step handler writes an exit value here; the game-over handler uses 1 for its state-restore exit. The system-step setter clears it to 0.
Per-step substate byte. The active step handler switches on it, and the step setter resets it to 0 through func_80003628_4228.
Per-step substate completion byte, cleared by the substate setter.
World-handler substate while main step is 13: 0 initializes the world, 1 handles ordinary gameplay/pause, 2 tears down the world.
Current room ID. The live destination consumer assigns it from the prepared destination; do not confuse it with +0x3AFE0.
Previous room ID preserved by the live destination consumer.
Native start-sequence gate. Zero is the cleared value used for normal gameplay; nonzero values must retain their native sequence meaning.
Player control mask (D_800C7AE0). Either low bit in mask 0x03 suspends the native late player collision handlers.
Player control/sequence lock. Nonzero retains native ownership; do not open another interactive prompt.
Scripted player input state (D_800C7AE3). The native move-toward and input-playback paths set it while supplying scripted input.
Native task execution/render mask. The task scheduler uses only low mask bits 0x0007; Start pause adds 0x0001 to suspend matching task subtrees.
Native Start pause/menu state. Zero is ordinary gameplay; nonzero dispatches the native pause overlay state machine.
Destination-transition marker; the warp destination helper writes 1.
Seventh argument of the warp destination helper; individual values are not yet interpreted.
Eighth argument of the warp destination helper; individual values are not yet interpreted.
Destination room/stage ID. Use the room table on D_800C7AB2.
Additional world/room-start busy gate checked by the ordinary gameplay pause path. Zero is required to begin another interactive operation.

tables.title: Known main-system steps
tables.description: These are selected established values of the byte at full-system offset +0x3ADD4. A step change depends on initialized native callbacks and related state; this is not a complete state-machine enum.
rows: Start/sequence step; loads overlay file 0x16. The native game-over goodbye exit and the ordinary world-teardown path both select it.
Ordinary world dispatcher; world substate at +0x3ADDE selects setup, gameplay/pause, or teardown.
Game-over handler; presents the continue/goodbye choice and exits to step 0x0B or step 0x03.

tables.title: Graphics-bank layout
tables.description: Offsets are relative to one bank, beginning at full system base + bank_index × 0x1D6D8. There are two banks; these fixed arrays are distinct from CPU task and display-record storage.
rows: Additional native workspace; individual fields are not interpreted here.
Additional native workspace; individual fields are not interpreted here.
Final native workspace, ending at bank offset 0x1D6D8.

tables.title: Interior-alias field offsets
tables.description: This exported byte array begins at full-system offset +0x30000. Use the alias-relative offset in this table when indexing D_800BCCC0_BD8C0 directly; adding a full-pointer offset to this alias addresses the wrong memory.
rows: Game-loop timing/control byte; the system-step setter writes 2.
VI counter used by the saved play-time accumulator. Native Start pause does not stop its VI increments.
Game-loop/frame counter; a running numeric counter, not a state ID.
Main-step completion/substate byte; the step setter clears it to 0.
Native start-sequence gate. Zero is the cleared value used for normal gameplay; nonzero values must retain their native sequence meaning.
Native task execution/render mask. The task scheduler uses only low mask bits 0x0007; Start pause adds 0x0001 to suspend matching task subtrees.
Native Start pause/menu state. Zero is ordinary gameplay; nonzero dispatches the native pause overlay state machine.
Destination-transition marker; the warp destination helper writes 1.
Seventh argument of the warp destination helper; individual values are not yet interpreted.
Eighth argument of the warp destination helper; individual values are not yet interpreted.
Destination room/stage ID. Use the room table on D_800C7AB2.

tables.title: Health units
tables.description: The native field is a signed 32-bit health count measured in half-hearts. These rows show the unit conversion; they are numeric quantities rather than distinct state-enum entries. Native new-save health is ten half-hearts and is copied into this runtime word during save activation.
rows: Five hearts; native new-save current health after activation.

tables.title: Current health and Tsurami gate
tables.description: This native current-health word is located at save-base offset -0x24; see the [save field layout](./D_8015C608_15D208.md#save-field-layout). Tsurami uses the word as a zero/nonzero gate before its private post-update body, rather than testing whether health is positive.
rows: Current health is zero; skip the gated Tsurami private post-update body.
Current health is nonzero; the gate allows the private post-update body. The native test is != 0, not > 0, and other callback conditions still apply.

tables.title: Actor instance fields
tables.description: Offsets are relative to the actor instance pointed to by this variable, not to the pointer storage. A null definition pointer terminates the instance list during native actor-manager traversal.
rows: Spawn position X, Y and Z.
Spawn rotation: pitch, yaw and roll.
Actor definition record; zero terminates the native instance list.
Spawn-state byte. A full raw-value interpretation is not established.

tables.title: Actor definition fields
tables.description: Offsets are relative to the definition record pointed to by the variable. Parameters and the three data words are actor-specific.
rows: Actor ID: indexes the entry-callback and actor metadata tables.
Three actor data words copied to task offsets +0xD0, +0xD4 and +0xD8 by the native initializer.

tables.title: Known actor IDs
tables.description: Selected actor IDs with established descriptive names. Names distinguish actor types and variants; they do not define the parameters or behavior of every instance.

tables.title: Dungeon key definition fields
tables.description: Applies to actor ID 0x193 only. Definition offsets are relative to the record pointed to by D_8015CDE0 during initialization; task offsets are relative to the initialized actor. func_80218A54_5D3F24 copies the definition payload as 32-bit words, preserving the big-endian byte and halfword fields below. The file_43 entry func_080001BC_6F369C checks the pickup flag and removes an already collected key. Its pickup callback func_0800058C_6F3A6C sets the same flag through func_80024038_24C38. [Verified pickup records](./D_8015C608_15D208.md#unresolved-save-flags) list all 29 mapped definitions.
rows: Packed save-flag ID recording this key pickup; not a byte offset or key count.

tables.title: Dungeon key colors and textures
tables.description: Native key color values correspond to the original game artwork below. Resource IDs and ROM offsets identify texture sheets. A verified D_ symbol identifies a mutable native texture-handle word, not the pixel address. Every crop is 24 by 24 pixels from a 64 by 32 RGBA5551 sheet. The silver and diamond sheet has no verified D_ handle mapping yet.

tables.title: Moving platform variants
tables.description: Actor 0x3E0 uses the byte at definition +0x04, copied to task +0xD0, to choose file_44 platform setup. The setup callback then repurposes several task data fields; the definition variant must be retained separately when interpreting live state.
rows: Alternates a pause with a half-turn in pitch; definition +0x08 selects rotation direction.
Timed pitch rotation; definition +0x05 is a nonzero duration byte and is used as a divisor.
Continuous pitch rotation at -8 angle units per native update.
Translates and rotates, periodically reversing its route.
Translates along a second route using the same state-machine family as variant 3.
Translates and rotates with alternating vertical direction.
Half-turn rotor with its initial delay read from definition +0x05.
Continuous pitch rotor using the same updater as variant 2.
Horizontal rectangular motion with four directional legs.
Sine-wave vertical motion; creates a moving child hazard each time the phase wraps.
Vertical rectangular motion with four directional legs.
Sine-wave motion; subtype definition +0x05 values 0 and 1 choose render/collision setup. Other subtypes enter the falling-platform setup.
Player-triggered falling platform; native standing-object and player-motion checks arm the fall. Restores its saved origin after a timer.
Orbit in the X/Y plane using stored origin, radius and angle.

tables.title: NPC path task fields
tables.description: These offsets belong to actors initialized with func_80226840_5E1D10 and stepped by func_802268A8_5E1D78. Route scripts can invoke dialogue and camera behavior; copying these scalar fields does not make executing a route safe in an unrelated actor or dialogue context.
rows: Path route ID; the US path table contains 163 entries.
Substate of the active path operation.
Instruction position measured in 16-bit words, not bytes. Only instruction boundaries are valid.
Facing value used by the path updater.
Native path initialization stores a self pointer; this is not transferable scalar state.

tables.title: World actor event boundaries
tables.description: Events below distinguish a real collection, break or emission from ordinary actor distance culling. They describe native behavior; callback entry alone is insufficient when the listed status or timer condition is absent.
rows: Awards 5 ryo and arms status +0x68 bit 0x2 for removal.
Heals by 2 and installs a removal continuation.
Heals by 40. The following cleanup signals the shine child at task +0xE4 and resets local player controls.
func_08000150_6B30F0 executes after the hit transition
Spawns definition-selected contents and proceeds to broken-container cleanup.
File_34 update observes its old task +0x8A countdown equal to zero
Emits one hazard and resets the countdown. Subtype byte at definition +0x08 selects the 150-tick or 50-tick cycle.

tables.title: Child actor common state
tables.description: Fields initialized or consumed by func_80218C28_5D40F8 and the common actor update. Offsets are relative to a live task, not its placed definition. A child can inherit its parent's entity number, so that number alone does not identify its behavior.
rows: Pre-update, AI continuation and post-update callbacks. Preserve disabled-callback tagging.
Primary display/transform object. func_80216CE0_5D21B0(task, object, model_slot) also binds linked objects, so its object argument must equal this pointer when observing the primary appearance.
Collision or target references; they are not portable scalar state.

Zero selects the ordinary body-only setup; 0xFFFFFFFF selects scalar attack dimensions. Otherwise func_80218DCC_5D429C binds an entry from the local model resource list. These modes must remain distinct.
Entity and model identities. Native child setup initially inherits these from the parent.
Behavior flags, auxiliary flags and transient status; status bit 0x2 requests removal and 0x200 marks pickup contact.

Shadow scale and offset. func_80219E70_5D5340 temporarily selects model 1 and calls func_80216E54_5D2324 with slot 0 to allocate and bind a separate linked shadow object, then restores the task model. Copying flags alone does not create the shadow.
Zero for ordinary child actors. Grouped placed actors use this for distance-culling and later respawn.
Task generation, gravity coefficient, grouped-culling delay and actor category respectively. Gravity subtracts coefficient / 50 from vertical velocity.
Motion velocity; the common motion step adds twice each component when flag 0x200 is enabled.
Continuation-specific countdown; meaning must be checked against the active native callback.
Local function pointer for NPC dialogue
The talk helper saves the current AI continuation here. A temporary wrapper must not become the dialogue return target.
Persistent shine child; setting its byte +0xD0 retires the shine. Full food cleanup also resets local player controls.

Texture speed, sequence selector, current index and frame delay for the first texture-animation track. func_80224ABC_5DFF8C initializes this track; common post steps it when task +0x60 bit 0x2 is set. Bit 0x4 loops at the end instead of clearing the selector. Coin lifetime uses the separate task +0x8A timer.

tables.title: Additional world mechanism state
tables.description: Native families with distinct continuation and private-state layouts. A platform-family layout must not be applied to unrelated mechanisms merely because they also move.
rows: Falling trap: wait, fall, delay, rise and rearm continuations in File_30.
Signed task +0xA0 retains the immutable return height; gravity coefficient +0x75 is initialized to 10.
Elevator in File_44, including calls from the opposite floor.
Task +0xE0 is a local route-table pointer. Idle compares endpoint Y and player Y against table values; riding alone is not its only trigger.
Signed +0xE4 is the oscillation amplitude (within -50 through 50). +0xE0 retains its native yaw reference.
Definition subtype 2 enables the common path VM using the route at +0xD6; validated path state must accompany a motion checkpoint.
Public position/velocity are distinct from +0xD0 through +0xDC local previous-position/contact work used for sound.
Wait reads temporary room flag 0, then switches to the rising continuation and mechanical sound.
func_08003410_6F68F0 arms removal only after the actual break. Subtypes 3 and 4 also set persistent flags 0x1C2 and 0x1C3.
Opening animation and mesh state accompany local travel logic.

func_801FB240_5B7150 locks local player control. The animation-complete continuation can set destination/travel fields; do not invoke it merely to reproduce another door's appearance. Task +0x60 bit 0x01000000 reverses skeletal playback; bit 0x1 enables the common animation step. Clear object +0x7C completion bit 0x2 to resume a completed clip. Nonlooping reverse playback clamps object +0x28 to zero. Entity 0x23A instead includes progression barriers with deletion callbacks.

Float task +0xDC is an integer cycle index 1 through 8. Rotation adds two angle units per update; at index * 128 it masks the angle to 10 bits and waits 30 updates before incrementing the index, wrapping 8 to 1. The signed +0x8A timer and continuation distinguish motion from waiting.

Idle compares its object with the local player task +0xA0 ground-object pointer. It moves along Z at -4 to -404, waits 60 updates, returns at +4 to Z=396, waits another 60 updates, then rearms. Native callbacks use exact endpoint equality.
Flag-driven staircase pieces in File_30; variants 0 through 11.

Task +0xD0 byte selects a native endpoint; +0xD4 unsigned halfword selects the temporary flag. func_08003418_6C2B68 starts motion with duration argument 120; func_080036E0_6C2E30 detects arrival and func_08003A74_6C31C4 clears velocity.
Save-flag-driven puzzle pieces in File_30; variants 0 through 7.

Task +0xD0 byte selects the endpoint; +0xD4 unsigned halfword selects the save flag. Variants 0/1 use distance-normalized velocity; variants 2–7 initialize linear motion with duration 121. func_080040B8_6C3808 writes the fixed endpoint and zeroes velocity. The initializer reads the save flag and schedules the endpoint continuation immediately when it is already set; this differs from arriving there through the motion continuation.
The initializer selects one of six local geometry slots. func_0800435C_6C3AAC only refreshes its native tint; it does not move a puzzle piece.

Byte +0xD8 zero starts immediately; otherwise wait for temporary bit (D8-1). 080026D0 selects static model using byte +0xD9, saves XYZ as +0xC8/+0xCA/+0xCC and subtracts 0x8000 from definition halfwords +0xD0/+0xD2/+0xD4/+0xD6 once. 08002788 and 08002820 alternate between origin and destination using speed D6/20. Byte +0xDA controls local start sound.
Fire-reactive moving platform with a child collider in File_44.

Word +0xD8 bit 2 gates the constructor on save flag 0x1A4; bit 1 starts its inactive mode. +0x9C is a local child task pointer. The child runs 08002DBC, follows its private float XYZ at +0xD0/+0xD4/+0xD8 and copies the local hitter pointer +0x38 into +0xDC. Parent +0xE2 states 0-5 track normal, fade, brighten, wait, reform and inactive; +0x8A holds 40/40/256/40 phase timers, and +0xEE holds the 10-update shake. +0xEC retains direction; +0xE0 supplies the tint angle. Floats +0xDC and +0xE4 supply red and green work. 08003074/08003148 move, 0800321C shakes, 0800329C advances melt/recovery.

Writes a local six-word display list at object +0x80 and packed RGBA at +0x8C, flushes its cache and returns object+0x80. Parent object +0x30 retains that local address. Fire-platform phases 2/3 do not update the tint, so their scalar color work alone cannot recover the visible tint. Rebuild the local list from the captured RGBA value; never transmit the list pointer.
Static File_44 geometry in all 33 examined placed records.

The sole placed definition has gate byte +0xD4 zero and flag-index byte +0xD5 four. 080001B8 binds the geometry with helper 08000000; its separate gated branch is not exercised by these placed records. Dynamic/script invocation of the gated branch remains separate audit work.
Rolling physics puzzle and reward producer in File_30.

Task +0xD0/+0xD4 retain prior X/Z velocity and unsigned halfword +0xDC is a throw countdown. 08006C18 skips its rolling/completion body when current health D_8015C5E4 is zero. Reaching -4<X<18, 103<Z<120, Y=8 zeroes velocity, sets status 0x80000 and enters shrink callback 08006F48, followed by animation 1, animation 2, then a 200-count reward callback 080070E4. That callback attempts a randomized native child each time the unsigned timer is divisible by 10, including zero before decrement, then schedules empty continuation 080072C4. Shrink multiplies all scales by 0.95 until X scale is at most 0.05, then resets scale to 0.2. Reward children use initializer 80214314 (coin) for random values below 80, otherwise 802141AC (health); launch speed is Y=5 and horizontal magnitude 0.9. The native parent/child builder owns local resources.
Task status +0x68 bit 0x8000 and local player work +0x8C.

func_801E54A8_5A13B8 stores the object task in player task +0x5C -> +0x8C and sets its held bit. func_801E55A0_5A14B0 clears both. func_801E55D4_5A14E4 sets throw velocity and pose before releasing. Carry callbacks can dereference the held task on throw; detaching alone does not end the player carry action. The pickup search also excludes task status 0x80000, which the completed puzzle sets.
Task +0x68 contact bits and +0x70 placed-source pointer.

func_8021C518_5D79E8 clears and recomputes status 0x1000/0x2000 from geometry results. func_8021A328_5D57F8 clears source +0x70 before proximity removal. Actual throw-break deletion retains the source. func_80218F30_5D4400 creates an empty cooldown task whose +0x76 enlarges the proximity box by five tenths; it releases the source only after leaving that box, rather than after a countdown.
File_30 root 0x1B9 creates four children, including the moving crane; root 0x1BB creates two pressure pads. The moving child has a nested X-position follower.

Children store their local parent task pointer at +0xDC; resource ID 0x1E and its local pointer are at +0x28/+0x2C. Roots do not retain a child-pointer array. Do not interpret these pointers as private scalar state.

Power flag 0x15A gates activation. Each pad lowers Y by 0.3 for eleven updates, waits for departure, and rises by 0.3 for eleven updates. The timer starts at ten and checks its old value before decrementing, so zero also moves.

The native trigger compares the pad object against local-player task +0xA0. Temporary bits 0/1 track held pads and 2/3 mark their return. These local-player comparisons do not describe another player standing on a pad.
Temporary bits 6/7/8/9 mark target, animation and return boundaries; bit 0xB marks the low crane region and bit 0xE latches a cycle.

Temporary bits 0xC/0xF instead select local occupancy and a one-time scene. Save bits 0x15B/0x15C are a reversible scene/camera handshake. Temporary 8 is write-only in File_30. Save 0x15E is written after animation completion and 0x15F at the upper Y clamp; no readers or clearers were found in the native helper-call and scenario-flag scan. They are historical milestones, not phase selectors.

The power switch sets save 0x15A through a local scenario/fade path. The camera controller owns a camera task at +0xD0. Placed 0x3D3 is the Wind-up Camera reward: it consumes temporary bits 6/7/9, then waits for task status +0x68 bit 0x200 before starting scenario 0x83 and setting consumed flag 0x1A3.

The 0x3D3 initializer deletes itself when 0x1A3 is already set. Scenario 0x83 independently writes one to save-base +0xC8 (camera owned) and +0xD8 (camera chargeable). The consumed flag alone does not grant those capabilities. Contact also starts local letterboxing and collision/model teardown; its final callback waits for local scenario cleanup. Task +0xDC is a local byte on 0x1BF, unlike the child-parent pointer there.
File_30 binds model 0x23F and animation 0xE; entity identity remains 0x354.

Signed timer +0x8A starts at 60, opens on its old zero value, waits for animation completion, then counts 90 before closing. At old timer 30, immutable word +0xD0 equal to one creates an effect and category-6 entity 0xFC; zero disables emission. The loop has no existing-child guard. Continuations are 08005624, 08005684, 080056FC and 080057D0.
File_32 initializer func_08001EA4_6D0F84 binds model 0xFB. Word +0xD4 equal to one skips ground placement; +0xD0=0x39 selects route 57 through its low halfword +0xD2.

The common child setup gives one HP at byte +0x8D. Base flags are 0x002E8261 plus local shadow bit 0x08000000 only when shadow allocation succeeds. The sole continuation func_08001FF4_6D10D4 advances a finite route with four movement legs and no timeout, then removes the actor without a death reward. Several generations may overlap. Route +0xC4, timer +0xC6, origin +0xC8/+0xCA/+0xCC, substate +0xCE, PC +0xCF, facing +0xAA and status bit 0x400 are scalar state. Pointer +0x9C is the local actor itself; shadow and display lists remain local.
func_80218350_5D3820 calls func_80218548_5D3A18 immediately when damage reaches zero HP; a return hook runs after death and loot side effects.

For the dynamic route-57 robot, an accepted ordinary hit requires status +0x68 bit 0x80, non-null local hitter +0x38 and clear status bit 1. Fast damage uses status bit 0x40000 and subtracts one HP first. Native surviving-hit bookkeeping clears 0x80, sets status bit 1 and byte +0x8C to 60. Fast death ignores +0x90, sets removal bit 2, and rolls at most one coin or health child. Word +0x64 bit 0x8000 suppresses only loot. Route completion bypasses this death path.
func_802130C8_5CE598 and func_8021332C_5CE7FC take (child task, child object), not an effect selector.

Create each with func_802171A8_5D2678(parent, initializer, 8), copy parent scale to its child object, then write selector byte +0x8E=3 or +0x8F=4 before its scheduled initializer. These non-attacking visual tasks live at most 25 updates and create short-lived smoke/trails. The ordinary branch plays sound 0x222; fast death skips this presentation. Coin and health children inherit entity +0x5C=0xFC and change only model +0x5E to one, so clip 4 versus 3 distinguishes their item kind.

File_51 binds model0x2CC. Low halfword of task+D4, copied from definition+8, supplies dialogue0x10E or0x110; H+D8 selects route0x44 or0x43. Save0 is the Super Pass prerequisite; save1 records bridge opening.

Accepted local pass dialogue sets temporary bit0, starting both movement routes. Route return2 sets temporary bit1. Return1 unconditionally clears local sequence lock D_800C7AE2 before rebuilding common NPC state; it must not be replayed on behalf of another player. Dialogue pointers+B4/+BC/+EC and blink byte+76 are local.
Super Pass Bridge guard restore boundary

Routes0x43/0x44 retain C4/C6/C8/CA/CC/CE/CF/AA, object pose and velocity, task +0x60 bit0 and status +0x68 bit0x400. Their exact live X/Z targets before the completion ground probe are route0x43 (-451,69) and route0x44 (-408,69); save1-at-entry instead places route0x43 at (-466,49) and route0x44 at (-416,49). Carry actual Y because common ground placement may lower it.

Apply a route checkpoint only from a stable File_51 callback with local conversation bit0x100 and accepted-result bit0x4000 clear. func_80221A90_5DCF60 is not an idempotent restore helper: it probes Y and appends a new shadow on every successful allocation. Reconstruct completed common-NPC scalars directly. Preserve the receiver's existing local shadow-allocation bit +0x60 mask0x08000000 over base0x12800761; do not copy that bit from another actor. Preserve an unowned D_800C7AE2 lock, and let return1 clear it only after a tracked successful local func_8022125C_5DC72C acquisition. Route init changes +0x9C from the middle-face selector to actor self; routes0x43/0x44 do not read it, while client-local blink reads only +0x90/+0xA0.
File_51 initializer func_08000600_70DD40 binds clip0/model0x240 at scale0.1010000035. The sole placed definition has H+D8=1 and H+DA=0.

Temporary bit1 enables native animation and plays sound0x15E once. A save1-at-entry constructor chooses its inert completed continuation without replaying that presentation. All local player/travel branches require H+DA nonzero and are unreachable for this placed definition.
File_51 initializer func_080006F8_70DE38 binds model0x311, slot0, scale1 and object position(0,0,-9).

It deletes the current task immediately if save1 is set; otherwise func_080006B4_70DDF4 deletes on temporary bit1. This graph creates no children, rewards, loot or damage tasks. Save1 is committed by native guard dialogue opcode0x8020, not by the overlay callbacks.

tables.title: Town NPC continuation state
tables.description: File_59 NPC state beyond the common path checkpoint. Offsets belong to native tasks; callback, texture and route pointers retain their local resource identity.
rows: Saved AI continuation during common dialogue.
func_80220FF0_5DC4C0 saves task +0x0C here. Dialogue task/target pointers at +0xBC and +0xEC belong to the local conversation.
Native idle increments nonzero values; at three it plays the entry effect and clears the word. This is not an allocation or scene pointer.
Town pickpocket: path idle, approach, return, delay and escape continuations.
The approach callback can remove 50 ryo from the local player. The escape callback can release native coin drops when hit; replaying it merely to draw another actor can duplicate gameplay effects.
Signed saved X/Z and chase countdown.
The idle state also temporarily interprets +0xD8 as a word-sized entry counter.
One of two immutable escape-route tables.
D_08001C50_71D6D0 contains 20 halfwords; D_08001C78_71D6F8 contains 28. A leading pair and final pair are sentinels. Native table selection is local, never a transferable memory address.
Halfword waypoint index, signed step, hit/escape state and stolen-ryo checkpoint.
Live waypoint indices are even: 2 through 16 for the short route, 2 through 24 for the long route; step is +2 or -2. Hit/escape state is 0 or 1.
Segmented open-eye, mouth and blink texture selectors.

func_80224CE0_5E01B0 installs these then binds the open-eye selector. This intentionally replaces the path initializer's self-target at +0x9C; do not unconditionally overwrite it with a task pointer afterward.

func_80224D50_5E0220 chooses a blink and restores the open-eye selector. func_8021A764_5D5C34 resolves selectors against object segment bases: bank 2 uses +0x38/segment 8; bank 1 uses +0x40/segment 9; bank 0 uses +0x48/segment A.
Path instructions set or clear this bit before advancing their substate; a continuation requires the matching bit without replacing local collision/contact or dialogue bits.

tables.title: Room switch continuations
tables.description: File_50 entity 0x226 one-way modes used by the US-ROM placed actor definitions. Temporary and save flags have distinct lifetimes.
rows: Unsigned halfword flag ID / unsigned byte mode.
Mode 0 sets a temporary room bit; mode 1 sets a save bit. The examined placed IDs are temporary 0 and save 0x194, 0x195 and 0x19D.
The initializer tests the unsigned byte at +0xD4 for 0/1 before comparing the entire big-endian word at that offset against 2/3.

Any word equal to 2 or 3 has a zero first byte, so it has already selected the one-way path. The separate timed/rearming continuations cannot be reached through this initializer, including with dynamically supplied definitions.
The local collision producer owns the hitter pointer at +0x38 and its attack type. A remote visual update must not fabricate that pointer.
Bind clip 0 in reverse, select pressed mesh state 1 at +0x6C and disable playback.
Task +0x60 bit 0x01000000 selects the reverse endpoint; mask 0x1 is cleared after binding. The native scale is 0.15.
Set the definition-selected temporary or save flag.
Task +0xBC is assigned the local settled continuation before the spark burst. It is a callback pointer, not an integer phase or counter.
Create six native entity 0x227 sparks, then continue through +0xBC.
The children have local angles spaced by 0xAA. Their fade continuation changes tint/scale and deletes them; it awards no health or currency.
Empty native continuation; the pressed mesh and flag remain set until their normal lifecycle changes.

tables.title: Travel and entrance scene lifetimes

tables.title: Gateway coupled scene lifetime
tables.description: US-ROM File_53 entity0x316 in room0x153 creates several visible children alongside local dialogue, player, camera and fade tasks. Their identities and allocation lifetimes differ from the durable completion flag.

A, B, NPC, mesh and decoration inherit entity0x316 through func_80218C28_5D40F8. Their callbacks may subsequently replace model +0x5E.
Entity ID alone does not distinguish roles in this graph. Root and child pointers remain local.
Both use model0x24E. A starts at static slot1, shakes and switches to looping clip0. B starts at static slot2, shakes for60 updates, rises0.74 for270 and2.5 for900.
Phase +0xD0 and shake counter +0xD8 are scalars; B also uses timer +0xD4. B creates the mesh without retaining a child pointer.
Uses routes0x41 and0x42, then moves through three explicit endpoints. Its pre-callback also opens dialogues, changes temporary flags and installs a dialogue continuation.
Replaying func_080007F4_70E8A4 is not a side-effect-free way to restore an existing visible NPC. Preserve locally allocated shadow state.
+0xC4 is unsigned-halfword route ID; +0xC6 signed timer; +0xC8/+0xCA/+0xCC signed origins; +0xCE/+0xCF state/program-counter bytes; +0xAA facing selector.
The +0x9C self pointer, +0xD8 root-phase pointer and +0xB4 continuation are local addresses, not route scalars.

Run func_08001BD0_70FC80 once in the owning scheduler slot. Common teardown clears object+0x2C, installs a five-update delay, then frees the mesh arrays and deletes the task. Ownership of the separate private0x80-byte allocation remains unresolved.
The visible NPC, A/B and mesh exchange these cues with local player scripts, dialogue, camera, HUD and screen fade.
This bank is a scene handshake. Copying it wholesale can advance local player control. Freezing a cue producer without resolving its local consumer can strand cleanup.

The root discards the player task pointer; observe it at func_0800037C_70E42C. It waits for visible milestones3 and16. Camera+0xE4 points into the root until phase2 caches the NPC object; camera+0xE0 remains dereferenced through phase6.

tables.title: Emitter and mechanism child lifetimes
tables.description: The US native actor graphs below couple a placed task to independently scheduled children. Each constructor, common post-update path and removal cause participates in the room state. Offsets refer to the task unless explicitly identified as object offsets.
rows: The placed emitter counts down before creating flying blades with its subtype and speed bytes. Both emitter and blades have one-hit incoming damage and may produce death loot. A blade flight timeout removes it without the kill reward.
Preserve successful-birth ordinals and distinguish damage from expiry. A child must not dereference a culled or reused parent task. Bind the model and animation only when the child is scheduled.

An invisible scheduler tests a random emission period. Successful births create model 0x12F children with a 90-tick lifetime, animation rate 64/256, and horizontal velocity 7.5. Facing uses the target object referenced by task+0x84.
The target is an object pointer, not a task pointer or portable identity. Keep local addresses local. Allocation failure does not create a child or advance the successful-birth sequence.

A falling block arms within radius 80, transitions through falling and fuse callbacks, and explodes on an accepted hit or fuse/proximity trigger. The explosion allocates four model 0x7E rings and eight particles. Its no-loot flag excludes the generic reward path.
Variants 4 and 8 are damaging rings; variants 1 and 2 are visual. The local sound and twelve-child fan-out belong to one explosion, including when a replica is reconstructed.

Visual rings subtract 0x30 alpha and scale by 1.2. Damaging rings subtract 2 alpha with minimum 2, scale by 1.005 and delete when the old 90-tick counter is zero. Every ring turns yaw by 32. Particles subtract 0x10 alpha and do not use ring yaw.

The counter post-decrement produces 91 updates from 90. Preserve double multiplication followed by float storage for the ring scales. Colour helper returns are local display-list pointers with tag bits, never network colour values.

Each of three placed roots creates six static model parts. Standing on an upper or lower part sets its root support bit; the highest selected slot determines speed. Upper and lower groups move in opposite directions within their native Y bounds.
Reconstruct all six child slots before accepting a restored root checkpoint. Preserve local standing/contact pointers, and combine scalar rider masks instead of copying pointers.
Gateway, Koryuta, Kihachi and the Gorgeous Music Castle scripts mix visible actors with private camera, dialogue and temporary-bit handshakes. Koryuta also emits damaging model 0x12D and 0xFA waves.

A visible pose is not the local scene controller. Keep dialogue, camera and handshake execution local; reconstruct visual models using verified resource recipes. Treat damaging waves separately from decorative presentation.
